subject: AcmeCorp - Follow-up: subprocessor list & SOC 2 status
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up from today — subprocessor list & next steps

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciated the candid discussion about AcmeCorp's data handling requirements and the upcoming procurement timeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Redwood status: SOC 2 Type II in scope, current certificate attached.
- Subprocessors: I attached our consolidated subprocessor list (cloud providers, telemetry vendors, analytics). Please see the short table on page 2 for data boundaries.
- Next steps we agreed on: you to share the vendor security questionnaire (VSA) and procurement timeline; we will return completed VSA and a detailed subprocessor data flow diagram by EOD Monday.

Questions for you: can you confirm whether AcmeCorp requires HIPAA Business Associate Agreement language, or is SOC/GDPR evidence sufficient for initial procurement? Also, is there a specific security contact we should submit the completed questionnaire to (procurement vs. security team)?

I'll loop in Aditya and Jonas for any technical clarifications — they can prepare the data flow diagram and redact any non-essential internal notes.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_subprocessors_v1.pdf, redwood_soc2_certificate_2026.pdf

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — subprocessor list & next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick recap and the attachments — helpful. A couple items from our side:

- We do require SOC 2 Type II evidence; HIPAA is only required for specific healthcare workloads (not in scope for the pilot). SOC doc looks good at a glance.
- I'll send the vendor security questionnaire as an attachment to this thread (procurement prefers the spreadsheet). Please complete and return to procurement@acmecorp.com.
- For the subprocessor list, can you call out any cross-border data transfers (EU -> US) and the specific cloud regions you host inference workloads in? Our security team needs that detail to evaluate data residency impact.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood shares any de-identified telemetry with third parties (e.g., Sentry, Datadog) and whether those are included in the attached subprocessor PDF?

Best,
Alice
Senior Security Program Manager | AcmeCorp
alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com

Attachment: vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 12:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — subprocessor list & next steps

Hi Alice,

Thanks — received the questionnaire. Quick answers inline below and we'll fill the spreadsheet end-to-end by Monday: 

- Cross-border transfers: By default our hosted offering routes inference traffic to the region closest to the customer. For AcmeCorp (US-based), production inference would be hosted in US regions (us-west, us-east). We do offer EU regions for EU customers; the subprocessor PDF indicates region mappings on p.3.
- Telemetry/third parties: We ship anonymized metrics and errors to Datadog for observability and to Sentry for runtime error grouping. No PII is included in those telemetry streams — we strip prompts/outputs before logging. These tools are listed in the subprocessor doc under "Monitoring & Observability."
- HIPAA: noted that not required for pilot. If that changes, we have a BAA template and can discuss scopes.

Action items we will deliver: completed vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx, a redacted data flow diagram (showing where customer prompt/response data is stored/processed), and a clear callout of the subprocessor roles that touch metadata vs. content data.

We'll attach the filled questionnaire to this thread and include the diagrams. If procurement needs a stamped SOC or additional evidence, let us know and we can route that through security.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments (to follow): vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (filled), data_flow_redacted_v1.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today — subprocessor list & next steps

Hi all,

Filing the technical notes requested:

- Cloud providers: primary compute/storage in AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1). We also support GCP (us-central1) and Azure on request; those are listed as optional regions in the PDF.
- Data residency: inference ephemeral cache lives on GPU nodes for the duration of the request and is not persisted. Long-term storage (logs/metrics) is in segregated buckets with retention settings configurable per-customer.
- Telemetry: Adapters to Datadog/Sentry receive aggregated, redacted telemetry; no raw prompts are forwarded. We can provide a filter sample used before telemetry emit.

@Jonas — can you attach the redacted data flow diagram and the filled questionnaire here so procurement has the completed artifacts?

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
